The $(item)Fission Reactor$() is certainly an uncommon sight in GregTech - both in theme, and how it works. But fear not, we are here to guide you with this multi-purpose big-brain multiblock!$(br2)The most important thing you should know is that the reactor is like a big thermal $(thing)battery-generator$(). You input proper fuel, and get $(thing)heat$() (just like EU/t) that gets stored in the reactor as $(thing)rising temperature$() (stored EU).

You can then transfer this heat to $(thing)coolant fluids$() for running turbines, or performing EBF-style crafting recipes.$(br2)Fission's gameplay loop is mostly about delicately balancing the heat generated by a fuel rod against how fast your reactor can cool itself down. Manage this correctly, and you'll have more power than you know what to do with!

pages.title: Fission Reactor
pages.text: Note the central column of $(thing)Fuel Holders$() and empty space for $(l:mars/fission#components)Components$() and $(l:mars/fission#holder)Material Holders$().

pages.title: Fission Mechanics
pages.text: The more fuel rods you have installed in the reactor, the $(thing)hotter$() it gets. And the hotter it is, the more heat it is able to transfer out to the coolant fluid and processable items.$(br2)But physics has its limits, and the reactor can only ever get $(italic)so hot$(), so don't install too many fuel rods.

But fear not! Should the heat level of the reactor border dangerous territory, the reactor enters an $(thing)automatic cooldown sequence$(), and won't start again until all heat has been safely dissipated.$(br2)It's quite slow, though, and that's valuable time you could be using to produce more power instead. This cooldown also $(l:mars/fission#damage)damages the fuel rod$(), making it produce less byproducts when it's depleted.

pages.title: Components
pages.text: In addition to the 5 $(item)Fuel Holders$(), you can install $(bold)up to 20$() $(item)Components$().$(br2)The stats of all installed components will simply be summed up, and that's it! No other fancy positioning required.

Components can influence the reactor in four different ways:$(br)$(li)Max Temperature (insulator)$(li)Object Holder$() (allows additional item inputs)$(li)Efficiency (fuel lasts longer)$(li)Throttle (slows down the reactions)$(br2)At the moment, you only have access to insulators and the $(l:mars/fission#holder)Object Holder$().

While a $(thing)hotter$() reactor makes steam and byproducts faster, it is also more demanding for the fuel rods. Each fuel rod has limited durability, and this scales linearly with the temperature.$(br2)As you need more fuel rods for the higher heat, this in effect makes the damage scale $(thing)quadratically$().

If you want to heat coolants the most efficiently, you'll use low temperature. But if you want faster fissile conversion, use as high a heat as the insulation allows.$(br2)To start off, you'll want to fill your fission reactor with $(item)Blue Ice$() or $(item)Framed AES Insulation$(), as those are the only two insulators you'll have access to after landing on Mars, but you'll want to upgrade to $(l:mars/mars_fauna#glacian_sheep)Framed Glacian Wool$() ASAP.

pages.title: Processing Recipes
pages.text: Fuel rods aren't the only item you can put in the reactor! Putting a $(item)Material Holder$() inside your reactor will allow it to do $(thing)Processing Recipes$() - Press $(item)U$() on a Material Holder to view the recipes in $(emi). You can do more recipes at once with more Material Holders. These recipes can affect the level of heat in the reactor or provide other outputs.

pages.title: Example
pages.text: The simplified math is as follows: with sufficient coolant fluid and a $(thing)100%$() heat fuel rod, the reactor will reach a temperature of about $(item)200$() $(t:Heat Units)$(6)HU$(). This can also be referred to as heat level, or just heat. Having $(italic)two$() $(thing)100%$() fuel rods is equal to $(italic)one$() $(thing)200%$() rod, and both lead to about $(item)400$() HU.

This is because the fuel rod generates $(item)200 $(t:Heat Units per Tick)$(6)HU/t$(). Coolant fluids are able to extract $(item)1 HU/t$() per $(thing)1 degree of heat$().$(br2)If the reactor's max heat is $(item)190$(), a $(thing)100%$() fuel rod will overheat it. You can increase this with the $(l:mars/fission#components)components$(), or alternatively $(l:mars/fission#holder)active coolants$() via the processing system. Each recipe has a heat impact.

For example, if the recipe's temperature is $(item)100$(), and impact $(thing)-10 HU/t$(), it is able to cool down the reactor by $(item)19 HU/t$() at $(thing)190$() degrees.$(br2)That makes it possible to run the reactor with lower max heat, and not overheat! If the temperature is below $(item)100$(), it won't run at all - just like how EBF recipes have limits.

To start off, get your hands on some $(item)Thorium$(). Remember to wear all the $(l:game_mechanics/hazards#hazmat)relevant PPE$(), as Thorium is $(l:game_mechanics/hazards#radioactive_materials)radioactive$(). Your space suit will protect you for a little while, but will also take damage while it's in your inventory.

Next, craft some empty $(thing)Fuel Rods$() and fill them with the $(item)Nuclear Fuel Factory$(). The rods are reusable, so you don't have to make too many. In fact, you might want to make just a single one for now.$(br2)You'll of course need a completed reactor, too.$(br2)Why just a single rod? Let's delve deep into the reactor mechanics in the next page.

pages.title: Depleted Fuel Rods
pages.text: After your first $(item)Thorium Fuel Rod$() has finished processing, the reactor will output a $(item)Depleted$() fuel rod. The $(thing)lifetime average heat$() number on your rod's tooltip will indicate how much "damage" the rod took from overheating - the lower the number this is, the better.

Output all Depleted Rods back into your $(item)Nuclear Fuel Factory$(), where it will refund the empty fuel rod as well as some $(thing)Waste$(). The waste product is what you're after, as the amount you receive will depend on its lifetime average heat.$(br2)In Thorium's case, the only thing you can use it for at the moment is crafting the next tier of fuel rod - $(l:mars/fission#uranium)Uranium$().

While Thorium rods don't produce much power, their real appeal is the $(item)Thorium Waste$() needed to produce $(item)Uranium Fuel Rods$(). Make sure you understand how the fission reactor works before moving on to these, as a reactor without any $(l:mars/fission#components)components$() won't be able to handle their heat of $(bold)435$().

At this point, you have three options for safely running Uranium rods:$(br)$(li)20x $(l:mars/fission#frames)Framed Glacian Wool$() will raise your maximum heat to $(bold)440$(). This solution is easiest but requires $(l:agriculture/animal_husbandry#wooly_animals)shearing$() a lot of $(l:mars/mars_fauna#glacian_sheep)Glacian Sheep$() first.$(br)$(li)Use $(l:mars/fission#holder)Material Holders$() and insert large amounts of $(item)Dry Ice$() to drop the reactor's temperature. You will want access to a $(thing)Liquid CO₂ Fluid Vein$() if you go this route.

$(li)Use $(item)Refrigerant Pellets$() in combination with $(l:mars/fission#holder)Material Holders$(). They behave like Dry Ice but are far more potent. Note that Refrigerant Pellets consume a decent amount of $(item)Fluorine$() to craft, and you do not have infinite Fluorine at this point.

Obviously, you can also make your own sauce and mix all of these options together. We recommend having separate rectors for both Thorium and Uranium, though in the future once you get better cooling capabilities you may be able to mix them together.$(br2)Make sure your steam turbines are ready too! Uranium rods last 4x as long but produce 5x more steam than Thorium.
Speaking of steam, the steam that Uranium rods output is a bit too spicy for your steam turbines to handle - you'll need to send it through a $(item)Heat Exchanger$() first.

Just like before, the main goal of Uranium rods is producing byproducts to make the next tier of fuel rods, in this case $(item)Plutonium$(). These are your final test - you'll need a reactor full of your best $(l:mars/fission#components)Passive$() and $(l:mars/fission#holder)Active$() cooling (such as $(item)TerraFirmaGuard PA6$()) in order to maximize your yields of the precious $(thing)Tritiated Water$().

pages.title: Fission on Earth
pages.text: Hungry for more Fission? Starting with the $(item)Thorium-Uranium Breeder Rod$(), you can produce other exciting kinds of fuel rods that also work on $(l:the_world)Earth$(). You will want a robust $(l:logistics/railgun)Railgun$() network to produce the rods on Mars and send them over to your main base, and in exchange you will have a difficult but rewarding power source for a long long time.

pages.title: Tips
pages.text: If you're struggling to send your steam around fast enough, try $(item)Tungsten-Bismuth Oxide$() or $(item)Tungsten Steel$() Fluid Pipes, or AE2's $(thing)Fluid P2P$().$(br2)Don't try to send it around through interfaces or buffer it in your ME Drives, it won't be fast enough!

Item Input Buses will always pull items from their indicated face.$(br2)Remember you can also input items through their other faces, where you will have more control over $(item)how items are input$().$(br2)Export Buses with Threshold Switches or even Create components can be useful here, along with other $(l:logistics/redstone_devices)redstone devices$().

Need to produce more Heavy Water?$(br2)Remember the Large Centrifuges can be overclocked to $(9)IV$(), and can also accept multi-amp hatches to go even faster.$(br2)Fission outputs a lot of energy, take advantage of it!
Finally, be sure to read the $(5)EV$() quests for fission as well! They go into much more depth about all the other steps in between each fuel rod, and overall progression.
